findings.title: Delete menu item never renders in V2 list view because of stale rulerRule gate
findings.body: The Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule && (...)`. In the new V2 list view paths (GrafanaGroupLoader / FilterView) `rulerRule` is always undefined, so even when `canDelete` resolves to true via the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` path, no Delete entry is ever rendered. Worse, the `handleDelete` prop supplied by `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` does not actually need the ruler rule (it just calls `showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`), so the gate should be removed for Delete. With all required permissions the menu still cannot be used to delete rules from the new list, which is a user-visible functional regression.

findings.title: Pause menu item never renders in V2 list view; Pause functionality lost
findings.body: The Pause (`MenuItemPauseRule`) item is gated by `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'`. `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(undefined)` is false, so the menu item is never rendered in the V2 list view, even when `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` reports Pause supported and allowed. Unlike Delete, Pause truly needs ruler-rule data, so this PR effectively disables pausing Grafana alerting rules from the new list. Either an alternative pause flow using only `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` data must be wired up or the action must remain available in this view; otherwise users with pause permission lose the ability to pause from this entry point.

findings.title: Silence drawer cannot open in V2 list view because rulerRule gate
findings.body: The `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is truthy, where `rule` is the optional `RulerRuleDTO`. In V2 list view `rule` is always undefined, so the drawer is never rendered even though `handleSilence` can flip `showSilenceDrawer` to true. As a result, the 'Silence notifications' item opens a click handler that does nothing. The companion `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` flag `canSilence` will report the action as available, so the menu makes a promise the component cannot keep.

findings.title: Test asserts the regression by locking the menu item count to 4
findings.body: The new test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' grants full alerting permissions (global + folder) and then asserts `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` covering only `silence`, `copyLink`, `duplicate`, and `export`. With `AlertingRuleDelete` granted, Delete should render. The test instead hard-codes the broken count, so it will silently fail or require editing whenever the Delete/Pause/Silence regressions are fixed. Either extend the assertions to cover Delete (and Pause/Silence for alerting rules) or comment that these entries are intentionally hidden behind a follow-up. As written the test acts as a regression lock-in rather than a capability check.

findings.title: Rule details link dropped the returnTo parameter, breaking back-navigation
findings.body: The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` builds the rule link with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` and no `returnTo` query parameter. The previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` passed `{ returnTo: createReturnTo() }` for the same link, and the existing `RuleActionsButtons` and other consumers rely on `createReturnTo()` to navigate back to the originating filtered/grouped list. Removing `returnTo` traps users on the rule details page when they came from the V2 list/filter view, which is a direct UX regression for anyone drilling into a rule from a filter.

findings.title: isProvisionedPromRule accepts PromRuleDTO but only returns true for Grafana variants
findings.body: `isProvisionedPromRule(promRule: PromRuleDTO)` always returns false for a non-Grafana `PromRuleDTO`, but the type signature suggests it applies to any prom rule. The companion `isProvisionedRule(rulerRule: RulerRuleDTO)` narrows with `isGrafanaRulerRule`. The new function should be similarly restricted (e.g. accept `GrafanaPromRuleDTO | undefined`) or documented, otherwise downstream callers (like `getIsProvisioned` in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) may believe they are checking provisioned state for cloud/prom rules when they will always get `false`.

findings.title: Loss of optimistic Creating/Deleting state tests not covered elsewhere
findings.body: The PR removes tests 'should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists' and 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists' together with the matching optimistic UI implementation. Nothing in the new suite asserts behavior for the eventual-consistency window between Ruler and Prometheus (rules that have just been created or are being deleted). With the new design relying solely on Prometheus, the absence of either end of that optimistic state should be confirmed explicitly (e.g., a test asserting that a rule created via Ruler but not yet visible in Prometheus simply does not appear) so the contract change is intentional and visible to future maintainers.
